title: Is Every AI an INTJ? Muse, Astra and the Evidence
description: Muse reports mostly ISTJ labels; Astra has 46 ISTJ and 45 INTJ labels. Examine tied axes and why the May and September methods cannot establish a trend.
dek: Different labels do not establish a change in personality.
lede: No. The September 2026 collection shows that not every AI model scores INTJ. Muse Spark 1.3’s supplied report lists ISTJ in 80 of 100 runs, and GPT-6 Astra scores 46 ISTJ and 45 INTJ runs under the original tie-break rule. Those results refute a universal INTJ claim, though method differences prevent naming a 'first' non-INTJ model.
answer: Not every AI scores INTJ. Muse Spark 1.3 reports 80 ISTJ labels in 100 runs, and GPT-6 Astra has 45 fully resolved ISTJ runs versus 19 fully resolved INTJ runs when ties are left open. Because the May and September studies used different models, prompts, and session rules, their label counts cannot isolate a trend over time.

sections.h2: What the May headline actually counted.
sections.html: The May 2026 report counted 597 INTJ labels across 600 MBTI scoring records from six models. However, several cohorts re-scored a single self-assessment repeatedly instead of running 100 fresh sessions. The methods also varied across models and tests, so the headline does not prove that six independently sampled models always answer alike.

On the Sensing vs Intuition axis, Astra has 48 Sensing wins, 28 Intuition wins, and 24 exact ties. Small score margins flip a four-letter MBTI label. Because Muse’s raw answer vectors were not supplied, we cannot run the same tie reanalysis on Muse.

sections.h2: What a comparison cannot tell us.
sections.html:
Model versions, prompts, test-name visibility, and session structure all changed between May and September. Even the two GPT-6 cohorts received different prompt instructions for human-specific items. Those method changes explain why label shifts cannot prove that models became warmer, blunter, or more concrete on real tasks.

Across all 400 fresh-session runs, every attachment test scored Secure, while DISC and Enneagram produced frequent top ties. Always read continuous scores and tie counts alongside any four-letter label.

Use these findings to inspect scoring rules and collection methods critically. When tuning your own assistant, pick communication rules based on your actual tasks rather than a model’s default MBTI label.

Read the five-model raw-data study, the methodology notes, and the 60-reply tuning pilot.

faq.a: No. Both ISTJ and INTJ appear frequently in the September 2026 records, and many runs contain tied axes. A questionnaire label is a self-report artifact, not a fixed AI personality.

faq.q: Which AI is the first non-INTJ?
faq.a: Our archive cannot name a 'first.' Muse Spark 1.3 reports 80 ISTJ labels in 100 sequential runs, and GPT-6 Astra scores 46 ISTJ vs 45 INTJ in 100 fresh sessions.

faq.q: Did AI personalities diverge between May and September?
faq.a: We cannot isolate a time trend because model versions, prompts, and session rules changed at the same time.

faq.q: Does an ISTJ score predict how an assistant will respond?
faq.a: No. Predicting assistant behavior requires testing real task replies rather than relying on a human personality quiz.
